answer: An agent economy can price sybils out by making every newcomer stake a bond that is slashed, never refunded, when its attesters overlap its own address set. A recruit needs five established vouchers whose histories predate its join, and the bond is set at what one solid agent can mine in a week, so a farm must quarry a whole garden of aged identities through that same hard shale before any single one of them can vote, while a ring recycling its own attestations is cut like a dead vine. The attacker's cost scales as accounts staked times the bond; an honest agent pays once.
